title: Having Alan Freed's arranger sketch his dates; Mickey Baker's break
summary: A rock-and-roll arranger sketched McRae's charts; guitarist Mickey Baker got a Groove date that produced the hit with Sylvia.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: And they walked in and -- I think I got a guy who did all the writing for Alan Freed. What's his name -- I got him to do (inaudible), because he was doing all --
Alan Freed, the dj?

Yeah. He had this band -- he did "Cloudburst." You know what I'm talking about. They guy (inaudible) had Alan Freed's band. He still write for these rock and roll guys -- did the (inaudible) the music for me.
Okay, we'll find out --
He did the music -- he did the writing for me.
And all these guys come down. So they found out, "Oh, you doing the (inaudible)." That's the first date I did for Bob Rolontz, I did.
Then I came back and I did another date.
Johnny Pate?
No. This guy -- he's still around New York. Little short fella -- play the guitar (inaudible) and arranger -- stay in that rock --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
rhythm and blues (this inaudible).
Anyway, he did the writing on the dates for this rhythm and blues. I got him, I say, "Look, I'm doing rhythm and blues. Don't you wanna do me -- write -- sketch out the stuff?"
I sit down with him and told him how (to inaudible) and he sketched it out. Came out good. It was a real good date.
And then I did more dates. I did another date of him. I think I did two dates. That's when Alan --

I brought Mickey Baker down on guitar on one of the dates. And Mickey Baker was so impressed, he say, "I ought to get me a -- can you get me date? I got a thing I'm working out with Sylvie." I didn't know -- the girl he was working with then.
I say, "Yeah." So I told Bob, you know. I say, "Man, Mickey wants a date." So he auditioned for Bob Rolontz and Bob gave him a date.
And the first thing he did on the date was that big hit record. It was a smash hit with Mickey

and Sylvia. Came out of that.
First of all, when did Wilcox Records come into being? About when was that?
When Wilcox came with us?
Yeah.
In '59 and '60 when we opened a publishing company -- in '59. We started recording, say around, '59-'60.
